newsitem.title: USA: Conn. Gov's new budget to lower spending - paper.
newsitem.headline: Conn. Gov's new budget to lower spending - paper.

text.p: Connecticut Gov. George Rowland on Thursday will propose a new state budget that is lower in actual dollars than current spending, Hartford Courant reported, citing administration officials.
The budget approved for this year totals $10.02 billion, though actual spending likely will be higher due to a surge in tax revenues, which also is expected to create a surplus.
Connecticut Policy and Economic Council, a non-partisan body, said the last time that state spending was cut on a year-to-year basis was 1960, the Courant said.

Rowland plans to include at least $425 million in tax cuts, with about $360 million in income tax reductions. They which include around $15 million of savings for about 110,000 senior citizens who now pay the state income taxes on Social Security benefits, the paper said.

Further, Connecticut's governor plans to propose a 5-cent a gallon reduction in the state gasoline tax. This would save drivers $65 million if it were to start on July 1, the first day of the state's fiscal year.
The planned budget might encouter resistance because Democrats control both houses of the legislature for the first time since the Republican governor took office.

Still, the newspaper quoted Sen. Kevin Sullivan, D-West Hartford, the top ranking official in the Senate, as saying that Democrats in that house would not try to raise spending above Rowland's plan, provided the spending cuts were not speculative or based on gimmicks.

Sullivan and Senate Majority Leader George Jpesen, D-Stamford, have said that a plan to save $176 million over two years by offering an early retirement package to state employees, which has yet to be approved, is an example of fiscal gimmickry, the Courant said.
